To calculate overlaps, remember that the Manders calculation provides a comparison in both directions: channel A in B (M1) or channel B in A (M2), so depending on what you want to look at, you need to ensure the right M column is chosen to be plotted. So, keep in mind which channel is which fluorescent protein, and which direction you are measuring to get the correct M column (and make sure you use the thresholded.M!)

The code for extracting the data and creating the plots is basically the same for each chunk, except the P/Z comparison for JMC306 which plots both M1 and M2 comparisons of channels 1 and 3 (pgl and znfx). So, I've only annotated this first chunk and the P/Z for the colocalization analysis.

Something I am considering doing is changing how the stats are plotted so they all use the same calculation as the P/Z overlap section. That method also seems better when it comes to how to display the significance values and you can easily hide the ns ones (Whereas the currently used version for all other graphs I've just been removing the comparison from the comparison list so it doesn't plot)


JMC306
pgl overlap in wago
```{r}
# Filter rows based on conditions (pulling out channel 1 vs channel 2 comparisons.. ie. fluorescence channel) and extract Strain (ie. RNAi)
C1C2_df <- combined_df %>%
  filter(grepl("^C1", Image.A) & grepl("^C2", Image.B)) %>%
  mutate(Strain = sub("^.*-(.*?)(_.+)?$", "\\1", Image.A))

#pulls out thresholded Manders coefficient values (M1 = channel 1 signal overlapping in channel 2) from the txt file for the analysis
C1C2_simp <- C1C2_df[,c(13,20)]

#####**In this list JMC306 is M01 because the labels on the images made in FIJI were in the wrong notation .. usually I do RNAiStrain_WormStrain but these were done WormStrain_RNAiStrain so the lines above that add the Strain annotation for the dataframe populate the M01s as JMC306. If these images are totally redone then ensure they all follow the appropiate naming convention so lines 52-54 above do the right thing
#####greyed out comparisons were non-specific and manually hashtagged out so they didn't get plotted
listforcomp = list(#c("L4440","C27"),
                   #c("L4440","D"),
                   #c("L4440","F13"),
                   #c("L4440","F46"),
                   c("L4440","JMC306")#,
                   #c("L4440","Y110"),
                   #c("L4440","Y111"),
                   #c("L4440","Y39")
                   )

#proper strain names for the plot so it doesn't just have our shorthand nomenclature
strain_labs=c("L4440","C27B7.5","D2005.4","F13D12.5",
                   "F46F11.1","M01H9.3","Y110A7A.15","Y111B2A.3","Y39A3CL.4")

#creating the plot
ggplot(C1C2_simp, aes(x=Strain, y=Thresholded.M1, fill=Strain)) + 
  geom_dotplot(
  binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", color=NA, alpha=0.5
  ) + 
  #ylim(0,1.2) +
  #these are just some aethestic changes to make the plots look a certain way
  theme_classic(base_family="sans") +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=6),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size=6),
        aspect.ratio = 0.35) +
  labs(title="pgl-1 overlap in wago-4",
       x="RNAi strain",
       y="Manders") +
  #R will plot things in alphabetical order, so this specifies the actual order we want it to display the data
  scale_x_discrete(limits=c("L4440","C27","D","F13",
                   "F46","JMC306","Y110"),#,"Y111","Y39"), 
                   labels=strain_labs) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=colours) +
  #the stat_summary lines are for drawing the median and 1 standard deviation (2 is the default number of deviations for the mean_sdl function), we adjust this to do just 1 by adding "fun.args = list(mult=1)"). The geom=tile draws the mean, the geom=errorbar adds the standard dev 
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "errorbar", color="black", width=0.25
  ) +
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "tile", width =0.5, height=0.02
  ) +
  #this does the statistical comparison we set up above in the list my_comparisons
  stat_compare_means(ref.group="L4440", method='t.test', 
                     label="p.signif", hide.ns=T, comparison=listforcomp) +
  #I think this guides thing is just removing the colour legend or something like that
  guides(fill=FALSE)

#saves the plot - make sure this is properly pointing to where you want it to save!
ggsave(file=paste0(directory,"\\RNAi_C1C2M1_coloc_withstats.svg"))

```

pgl/znfx overlap
```{r}
strain_labs=c("L4440","C27B7.5","D2005.4","F13D12.5","F46F11.1","M01H9.3","Y110A7A.15","Y111B2A.3","Y39A3CL.4", "F56C9.6","Y66D12A.19","W05F2.6")

# Filter rows based on conditions and extract Strain
C1C3_df <- combined_df %>%
  filter(grepl("^C1", Image.A) & grepl("^C3", Image.B)) %>%
  mutate(Strain = case_when(
    grepl("L4440", Image.A) ~ "L4440",
    grepl("C27", Image.A)   ~ "C27B7.5",
    grepl("D", Image.A)     ~ "D2005.4",
    grepl("F13", Image.A)   ~ "F13D12.5",
    grepl("F46", Image.A)   ~ "F46F11.1",
    grepl("M01", Image.A)   ~ "M01H9.3",
    grepl("Y110", Image.A)  ~ "Y110A7A.15",
    grepl("Y111", Image.A)  ~ "Y111B2A.3",
    grepl("Y39", Image.A)   ~ "Y39A3CL.4",
    grepl("F56", Image.A)   ~ "F56C9.6",
    grepl("Y66", Image.A)   ~ "Y66D12A.19",
    grepl("W05", Image.A)   ~ "W05F2.6",
    TRUE                    ~ NA_character_
  ))

M1 <- C1C3_df[,c(13,20)]
M1$version<-"PGL-1 in ZNFX-1"
names(M1)[names(M1)=="Thresholded.M1"]<- 'Manders'
M2 <- C1C3_df[,c(14,20)]
M2$version<-"ZNFX-1 in PGL-1"
names(M2)[names(M2)=="Thresholded.M2"]<- 'Manders'

C1C3_simp <- rbind(M1,M2)

C1C3_simp$Strain <- factor(C1C3_simp$Strain, levels=c("L4440","C27B7.5","D2005.4","F13D12.5","F46F11.1","M01H9.3","Y110A7A.15","Y111B2A.3","Y39A3CL.4", "F56C9.6","Y66D12A.19","W05F2.6"))

stat.test <- C1C3_simp %>%
  group_by(version) %>%
  t_test(Manders ~ Strain, ref.group = "L4440") %>%
  mutate(p.signif = case_when(
    p < 0.0001 ~ "****",
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01 ~ "**",
    p < 0.05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ "ns"
  ))

stat.test <- stat.test %>% add_xy_position(x="Strain", group="version")

dodge <- position_dodge(0.6)

# Plot with modified x-axis variable
ggplot(C1C3_simp, aes(x = Strain, y = Manders, fill=version)) + 
  geom_dotplot(
  binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", color=NA, alpha=0.5, position = dodge
  ) + 
  #ylim(0,2) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "sans") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
        aspect.ratio = 0.35,
        legend.title=element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "pgl-1 znfx-1 overlap",
       x = "RNAi strain",
       y = "Manders") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_x_discrete(
  limits = names(strain_labs),  # ensures no gaps at edges
  labels = strain_labs,
  expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))  # tight padding, adjust 0.05 if needed
) +
  scale_fill_manual(values= c("#65A2B8","#EB5827")) +
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "errorbar", color="black", width=0.25, position = position_dodge(0.6)
  ) +
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "tile", width =0.5, height=0.02, position = position_dodge(0.6)
  ) +
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat.test, 
    label = "p.signif", 
    hide.ns = TRUE, 
    remove.bracket = TRUE,
    step.group.by = "version",
    y.position = max(C1C3_simp$Manders) + 0.05  # Set a position for p-values on top of the data
  )
ggsave(file=paste0(directory,"\\Whole_RNAi_C1C3_coloc_withstats.svg"))

```

granule count and size
```{r}
#point to where to find the granule Measurement files
meas_directory <- "C:/Users/fuent/Claycomb Lab Dropbox/Claycomb Lab Team Folder/Sebastian Fuentes/Grad School/Reasearch Project/Images/gg_Imaging/Compiled Data//"

meas_directory_save <-"C:/Users/fuent/Claycomb Lab Dropbox/Claycomb Lab Team Folder/Sebastian Fuentes/Grad School/Reasearch Project/Images/gg_Imaging/Compiled Dataplots//"
```

```{r}
#as said earlier, this is the colour list per RNAi strain and will likely need to be updated (the brood size count code probably has the most up to date colour list)
colours <- c("#4A6670", "#823038", "#D5A021", "#668F80","#A4A518","#1E000E","#EA5F44", "#D6A2AD", "#A0AF84","#222E50","#C12B01","#674ea7")

#specifying the statistical comparisons we want to make for each of the granule types, if its hashtagged out it means it wasn't significant so we removed it from being plotted
wago4_count = comparisons

wago4_size = comparisons

pgl1_count = comparisons

pgl1_size = comparisons

znfx1_count = comparisons

znfx1_size = comparisons

#setting up lists to use a loop to analyze everything
#grans is a way to type the gene/protein name without the hyphen because I won't want it to accidentally mess with the code when I stick that info in to any new dataframes/variables/etc
grans=c("wago4","pgl1","znfx1")
#how the genes were labelled in the txt files with the measurement info (we used a hyphen)
gran_list=c("wago-4","pgl-1","znfx-1")

strain_labs <- c("Empty Vector","C27B7.5","D2005.4","F13D12.5", "F46F11.1","F56C9.6","M01H9.3","W05F2.6","Y110A7A.15","Y111B2A.3","Y39A3CL.4","Y66D12A.19")

#loop time!
for (g in 1:3) {

  # List all files containing for example "wago-4" in their name
  meas_file_list <- list.files(meas_directory, pattern = gran_list[g], full.names = TRUE)

  # Create an empty list to store dataframes
  meas_list <- list()

  # Read each file and store it in df_list
  for (file in meas_file_list) {
    # Extract the prefix after "granules\\" and before the first underscore in the file name
    prefix <- sub(".*Compiled Data[\\\\/]+([^_/]+)_.*", "\\1", file)
  
    # Extract the Worm number after "_Worm" and before the next underscore
    worm <- sub(".*_Worm(\\d+)_.*", "\\1", file)
  
    # Extract the Nucleus number after "_n" and before the next underscore
    nucleus <- sub(".*_n(\\d+)_.*", "\\1", file)
  
    # Read the file into a dataframe
    df <- fread(file, sep="\t")
  
    # Add new columns with the extracted values
    df[, c("strain", "worm", "nucleus") := list(prefix, worm, nucleus)]
  
  # Append the dataframe to df_list
    meas_list[[length(meas_list) + 1]] <- df
  }

  # Combine all dataframes in df_list into a single dataframe
  ind_combined_df <- rbindlist(meas_list)

  sized_df <- ind_combined_df[ind_combined_df$Area >= 0.1,]

  # Define the lists of values for strain, worm, and nucleus
  strains <- c("L4440", "C27", "D", "F13", "F46", "F56", "M01", "W05", "Y110", "Y111", "Y39", "Y66")

  # Create an empty dataframe to store the counts
  count_df <- data.frame(Strain = character(),
                       Worm = integer(),
                       Nucleus = integer(),
                       Count = integer(),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  #this is used to set the size of the tile we plot in the stat_summary line below
  sized_y_range <- max(sized_df$Area)-min(sized_df$Area)
  sized_tile_height <- 0.02 * sized_y_range
  # Nested for loops to iterate over each combination of strain, worm, and nucleus values
  for (strain in strains) {
    comp_list <- get(paste0(grans[g],"_size"))
    #create a plot of granule size
    ggplot(sized_df, aes(x=strain, y=Area, fill=strain)) + 
    geom_dotplot(
    binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", color=NA, alpha=0.5
    ) + 
      #currently hashtagged out ylim which just specifies the y axis range, changing this range could help fit in more significance annotations if necessary
    #ylim(0,1) +
    theme_classic(base_family="sans") +
    theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=6),
          axis.text.y=element_text(size=6),
          aspect.ratio = 0.35) +
    labs(title=paste(gran_list[g]," granule size"),
         x="RNAi strain",
        y="area") +
      #R likes to go in alpha order, but we want it in this order
    scale_x_discrete(limits=c("L4440", "C27", "D", "F13", "F46", "F56", "M01", "W05", "Y110", "Y111", "Y39", "Y66"), 
                   labels=strain_labs) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=colours) +
      #same stat stuff we do with all the other graphs
    stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "errorbar", color="black", width=0.25
  ) +
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "tile", width =0.5, height=sized_tile_height
    ) +
    stat_compare_means(ref.group="L4440", method='t.test', 
                     label="p.signif", hide.ns=T, comparison=comp_list)+
    guides(fill=F)
    #save the plot! Currently it will save them within a "plots" folder wherever the Measurements text files are
    ggsave(filename=paste0(meas_directory_save,"plots\\RNAi_",gran_list[g],"_gransize.svg"))
    #now need to go into the details of how many granules per nucleus per worm to get an idea if number of granules changes
    for (w in 1:3) { #by worm
      for (n in 1:3) { #by nucleus
      # Count the number of rows that fulfill the conditions (ie. count the granules on a nucleus per worm per strain basis)
        count <- sum(sized_df$strain == strain & sized_df$worm == w & sized_df$nucleus == n)
      
        # Append the count to the dataframe
        count_df <- rbind(count_df, data.frame(Strain = strain,
                                              Worm = w,
                                              Nucleus = n,
                                              Count = count))
     }
   }
  }
  #this is used to set the size of the tile we plot in the stat_summary line below
  count_y_range <- max(count_df$Count) - min(count_df$Count)
  count_tile_height <- 0.02 * count_y_range

  comp_list <- get(paste0(grans[g],"_count"))
  #make a plot of the granule count!                                
  ggplot(count_df, aes(x=Strain, y=Count, fill=Strain)) + 
    geom_dotplot(
    binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center", color=NA, alpha=0.5
    ) + 
    #ylim(0,1) +
    theme_classic(base_family="sans") +
    theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=6),
          axis.text.y=element_text(size=6),
          aspect.ratio = 0.35) +
    labs(title=paste(gran_list[g]," granule count"),
         x="RNAi strain",
        y="count") +
    scale_x_discrete(limits=c("L4440", "C27", "D", "F13", "F46", "F56", "M01", "W05", "Y110", "Y111", "Y39", "Y66"), 
                   labels=strain_labs) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=colours) +
    stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "errorbar", color="black", width=0.25
  ) +
  stat_summary(
   fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult=1), 
    geom = "tile", width =0.5, height=count_tile_height
    )  +
    stat_compare_means(ref.group="L4440", method='t.test', 
                     label="p.signif", hide.ns=T, comparison=comp_list)+
    guides(fill="none")

    ggsave(filename=paste0(meas_directory_save,"plots\\RNAi_",gran_list[g],"_grancount.svg"))


}
```
